messages.subject: Density Equation Confirmation
parts:
Distance Users,

I would like to comfirm that I am using the correct density equation
within a paper I am currently working on.

Keeping in mind:

I was measuring the density of clustered populations
I was only recording data on one side of the transect line
I used a uniform key model with a simple polynomial adjustment

therefore D=n*s/Lu

d=density
n= number of groups detected
s= mean size of clusters
L= totallength of transects
u= effective width strip

I would appreciate any comments. Thank you.

Pamela

messages.subject: Re: Density Equation Confirmation
parts:
On Sat, 18 Sep 1999 17:48:13 -0400 (EDT), Pamela McRae wrote:

> >I would like to comfirm that I am using the correct density equation
> >within a paper I am currently working on.

> >Keeping in mind:
> >
> > I was measuring the density of clustered populations
> > I was only recording data on one side of the transect line
> > I used a uniform key model with a simple polynomial adjustment

This last bit of information was not necessary to answer the question - it
doesn't matter what key or adjustment you used - the formula is the same.

> >therefore D=n*s/Lu
> >
> >d=density
> >n= number of groups detected
> >s= mean size of clusters

By using mean cluster size you assume you don't have size bias (Distance
Sampling book, p77-87).

> >L= totallength of transects
> >u= effective width strip

Although we usually call mu (u) the effective strip width, it is actually the
effective strip half-width which is why your equation is correct.
> >I would appreciate any comments. Thank you.

My comment is that I think this question was a bit easy for sending to the
list - you could have answered it by looking in the Distance Sampling book,
which is available for free online. Perhaps next time you could consult
someone close to hand (if possible - e.g., Mark Ridgeway in your case) before
broadcasting your request to about 500 people on the list. However, this is
just my opinion, and I'm probabily biased as I work with this stuff every
day!

All the best,

- Len Thomas
